mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the prior month signals active monetary easing, compressing discount rates and increasing equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions and heightened recession risk, triggering equity sell-offs and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE rises above 4.0% within a 3-month window, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in UNRATE signals coordinated monetary policy response to labor market deterioration, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate policy support.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25pp and UNRATE rises by at least 0.1pp over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.04 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1400 thousand units, the S&P 500 tends to decline over the next 20 trading days, and this negative effect is amplified during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), producing more negative returns than in non-tightening regimes.
failure_condition: The average 20-day return following HOUST < 1400 is not significantly more negative in FEDFUNDS > 4.5% periods than in FEDFUNDS <= 4.5% periods (t-test p>0.05) or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the prior month signals weakening labor demand and reduced consumer spending power, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS declines by at least 50 thousand over the prior month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.04 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 (index base 2017=100) signals manufacturing sector contraction, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO falls below 100, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real GDP (GDPC1) from the previous quarter combined with rising inflation (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%) signals stagflation, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors price in growth slowdown and inflationary pressures.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 declines from prior quarter and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform over the next 20 trading days, and this negative effect is amplified when inflation is accelerating (CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.2% in the prior month).
failure_condition: The average 20-day return in CPIAUCSL > 3.0% periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05) or the negative effect is not amplified in accelerating inflation periods (t-test p>0.05 for the difference in returns between accelerating and non-accelerating high-inflation periods).
